To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) TDP2 catalytic activity is required for enterovirus infections in human cells, 2) TDP2 is required for efficient viral RNA synthesis in the absence of VPg, and 3) TDP2 activity is required for normal levels of positive-strand RNA production, but not negative-strand RNA production.
TDP2/ VPg unlinkase is required for efficient picornavirus infections at early times, but is dispensable at later times.

TDP2/ VPg unlinkase is not required for efficient enterovirus replication in hRPE-1 cells, and that the delay in virus growth kinetics is likely due to the requirement for TDP2/TPg unlinkase activity for efficient negative-strand RNA synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the host cell protein TDP2 affects the picornavirus life cycle.
the role of TDP2 unlinkase activity in picornavirus replication and provides a new model to study this process in human cells.
the identification of the step in the picornavirus replication cycle that is most affected by the absence of Tdp2/VPgunlinkase activity, and we have identified a likely candidate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VPg unlinkase (TDP2/5′ phosphodieterase) is not absolutely required for enterovirus infection, but that it does play an important, although not essential role in the early stages of infection.

the removal of VPgs from the RNA genome by TDP2/Unlinkase activity is required to allow the virus to efficiently transition from the initial round of virus translation to the next step in the virus replication cycle.

VPg unlinkase catalytic activity is required for picornavirus replication in a human cell culture model, and that it is likely required to facilitate the transition between the initial round of virus translation and the subsequent rounds of RNA replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VPg unlinkase is required to remove VPg from viral RNA to allow efficient replication and virus growth.
the presence of the VPg on the genomic RNA of picornaviruses is detrimental to virus replication, and TDP2/ VPg unlinkase removes VPg from the viral RNA to allow efficient replication to proceed.
the presence of a small peptide (VPg) on the RNA genome of picornaviruses has the ability to interfere with RNA replication and that the TDP2/ VPg unlinkase is required to remove this interference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of VPg unlinkage in picornavirus infection is more nuanced than previously thought.
the role of TDP2 activity in the picornavirus life cycle appears to be more complex than previously thought.
TDP2/ VPg unlinkase is a key host factor for efficient picornavirus infections, but its activity is not essential for virus replication.
